title: In-Car Gaming
subtitle: Bringing Cloud Gaming to the Smart Cockpit
summary: An in-vehicle cloud gaming experience developed through research, OEM integration, interaction exploration and a multi-screen consumer platform.
body: An in-car display is not an ordinary screen. Seat position, reach, input devices and the surrounding environment reshape how people discover and play. The platform was developed in cooperation with car companies and mobility partners including BMW, Dongfeng Nissan, Zeekr and Huawei. This case study follows the project in its original iteration sequence—from research and an OEM-integrated 1.0, through the unreleased 1.5 exploration, to the broader 2.0 platform system.

sections.title: Start by Asking the Right Question
sections.body: Before drawing a cockpit interface, the project first defined who would use it, where they would sit, what they could reach and which devices could actually control a game.

blocks.title: Direction B · Focus logic
blocks.body: A diagonal card layout has no square adjacency: pushing right could mean upper-right or lower-right. The ambiguity had to become an explicit focus rule.

blocks.title: Joystick direction fitting
blocks.body: That mapping could not be settled on paper — a physical joystick rig and live direction code were built to fit each raw stick movement to the card players actually intended, before any user session.

sections.title: From an In-Car Feature to a Consumer Platform
sections.body: From content and themes to touch and gamepad, version 2.0 expanded a single OEM feature into a consumer platform. One interaction system now spans screen formats, input methods, service operations, store and membership.

items.label: PERFORMANCE
items.title: Diagonal cards cost performance
items.body: The project returned to rectangular grids on the target hardware.

items.label: TO B → TO C
items.title: From owners to players
items.body: Operations, store and membership became necessary.

items.label: PLATFORM
items.title: Mobile and console coexist
items.body: Duration, quality and entitlement rules must remain legible.

items.label: INTERACTION
items.title: Input is not fixed
items.body: Touch, gamepad, keyboard, remote, voice and phone share one model.

blocks.title: 01 · From switching sides to always within reach.
blocks.body: The 1.0 gesture shortened reach but had to be discovered. In 2.0, both navigation rails stay visible with synchronised selection.

blocks.title: 03 · Navigation stays fixed. Content expands.
blocks.body: Screens vary widely across OEMs. Adaptation locks navigation and lets the content layer respond to the available width and height.

blocks.title: 04 · System entries stay put. Content expands.
blocks.body: Profile and search hold the top and bottom; the centre belongs to featured and library content. Entering All Games expands category tabs on the same structure, driven identically by touch and gamepad.

blocks.title: 05 · The UI steps back. The cabin joins in.
blocks.body: On entry the interface recedes so the artwork leads. On the next interaction controls return — together with the cockpit capabilities each game can drive.

items.body: On entry the system UI fades outward so the trailer or key art plays as the content; the next interaction fades it back in.

blocks.title: 06 · Expand from a source. Keep the origin.
blocks.body: Profile, search and messages expand from the sidebar with the origin fixed left. In game, the floating tool follows the same rule: a small entry expands into quality, virtual-controller and instruction settings without leaving the session.

items.alt: Profile hierarchy
items.label: PROFILE · THREE LEVELS
items.body: Account functions run three levels deep from one source, the back button marking each step; a flat card layout keeps them reachable.

items.alt: Search hierarchy
items.label: SEARCH
items.body: History, live results and an empty state — a quick entry that sits alongside browsing rather than replacing it.

items.alt: In-game floating tool
items.label: IN-GAME TOOL
items.body: A floating ball opens image quality and instructions during play, shown for members and non-members alike.

items.alt: Confirmation dialogs
items.label: DIALOGS · THREE SIZES
items.body: Small for queue, game switching, network checks and sign-out; medium for authorised login; large for agreements and custom-experience clips.

blocks.title: 07 · Going consumer means building a store.
blocks.body: The clearest result of the To B → To C shift is a store separate from profile, carrying membership, hardware and reserved operational slots.

items.body: The store carries membership, gamepad sales and reserved slots; an active member sees expiry, renewal and the five VIP benefits.

blocks.title: 08 · The cabin changes light. The structure does not.
blocks.body: Day and night in a moving cabin are not a style choice — the theme has to follow the vehicle system so the screen never fights the driver's eyes. Dark is the default immersive mode; both themes carry the same structure and hierarchy.

blocks.title: 09 · The account continues on the phone.
blocks.aside: Once the car account is linked, the phone app becomes the membership entry: sign in with WeChat or QQ, check benefits and membership status, and top up before the next trip.
